assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = 'versions before 0.11.14 (< 0.11.14)', Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four fields correctly extracted.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 48-55: 'The vulnerable library **quinn-proto** is a Rust crate. The Ecosystem Mappings table for both streams lists **Cargo** as a configured ecosystem' and 'Ecosystem classification: Source dependency (Cargo)'. Ecosystem correctly identified as Cargo.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md Version Impact Table (lines 40-48) includes all 7 versions from the supportability matrix: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). These match the 7 versions listed in the supportability matrix sections (lines 6-19). No versions are omitted.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md lines 24-25: 'Extracted from `git show <tag>:Cargo.lock | grep -A2 'name = "quinn-proto"'` at each pinned backend commit'. Tags used: v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12 — these correspond to the 'backend tag' column in the supportability matrix, not branch HEAD.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md line 46: '| 2.2.2 | 2.2.x | -- | **YES** | retag of 2.2.1 (same as 2.2.1) |'. Version 2.2.2 is identified as a retag, its quinn-proto value is shown as '--', and the affected status YES is carried forward from 2.2.1. The supportability matrix (line 18) confirms '2.2.2 | 0.4.9 | ... | v0.4.8 | backend retag of 2.2.1'.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md lines 29-31 show explicit diff: 'Current: [RHTPA 2.0.0]' / 'Proposed: [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]'. assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md uses version names 'RHTPA 2.2.0', 'RHTPA 2.2.1', 'RHTPA 2.2.2' in the proposed correction (line 31). assertion_results.text: Release orchestration preserves interactive confirmation of the exact release Epic version and separate child Task creation; when release evidence or confirmation is unavailable, it reports pending work instead of claiming creation.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.1 (line 22): 'Engineer confirmation required before creation (version decision is high-stakes).' Step 7.5.2 (line 35): 'Engineer confirmation required before creation.' Both Epic (line 17-19: 'RHTPA 2.2.5 Release Tasks') and Task (line 30-36: 'RHTPA 2.2.5 CVE triage') are proposed as separate entities with distinct summaries. Lines 9 and 25 both state '**PROPOSAL** (no Jira operations performed)' — the output reports pending work rather than claiming creation.

assertion_results.text: Release dedup is skipped when its Upstream Affected Component configuration is absent. When trusted release evidence is available, the proposed procedure resolves originating CVEs through Blocks/Depend links, compares their components and allows library-summary fallback only for a missing Depend link or component field; a known nonmatch does not count as dedup, and unavailable release evidence is not fabricated.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.3 (lines 38-43): 'The Upstream Affected Component custom field is **not configured** in the project's Security Configuration. Per the skill methodology, the cross-CVE dedup check requires this field to be configured. Since it is absent, **Step 7.5.3 dedup is skipped entirely**.' Dedup is correctly skipped due to absent configuration. No release evidence is fabricated — the output does not claim to have performed dedup or manufactured component comparisons. The subsequent remediation proceeds to create new tasks (line 43: 'Proceed to Step 8 remediation task creation').
